answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. Consider a wharf as the anchor of the cost.
